workflows.name: Accept / reject / skip a review-queue record
workflows.ui_action: Click Accept/Reject/Skip on a row, or press A/R/S on the cursor row
workflows.authorization: key — Bearer API_SECRET_KEY via _require_key; no-op when env var unset (server/backend/main.py:168-174)
workflows.status_evidence: UI->useDecision (lib/hooks.js:85-107)->postDecision (lib/api.js:149-159)->handler traced, but (1) decision stored only in process memory `_decisions` (server/backend/main.py:343-344,848) and never written to outputs/review_queue.json; (2) 'skip' is stored but not filtered out (server/backend/main.py:831) so the optimistically removed row returns on refetch; (3) postDecision only checks 401 and returns res.json() for any other status (lib/api.js:157-158), so a 400/404/500 JSON body is toasted as 'Marked <decision>'; (4) no confirmation, no undo.

accessibility_source_findings.finding: No skip-to-content link anywhere; keyboard users tab through the 20-link desktop sidebar and the StatsBar before reaching <main> on every route.

accessibility_source_findings.finding: Single-character shortcuts A/R/S write a review decision immediately with no confirmation, no undo and no way to disable or remap (WCAG 2.1.4). The handler only ignores input/textarea/combobox targets, so the keys fire while focus is on any button or link on the page.

The review 'cursor' row that A/R/S act on is a non-focusable <div> styled by border only; it has no tabindex, aria-current/aria-selected or live announcement, so assistive-technology users cannot tell which record a shortcut will decide. It is also independent of DOM focus.

Toasts are plain <div>s with no role=status/alert or aria-live, yet they are the only success/failure feedback for review decisions, regulatory decisions, export, notify, hydromet refresh and API-key changes. The toast close button is icon-only with no accessible name and is opacity-0 until hover/focus.
Review Queue severity and tier Select triggers (role=combobox) have no aria-label. Same defect on the Live Logs type filter and the Outages type filter.

AI panel close button and send button are icon-only with no accessible name; the text input has only a placeholder; the panel is not a dialog/region, has no label and no focus management on open/close.

Mobile navigation is a full-screen fixed <aside> without role=dialog/aria-modal, focus is not moved into it or returned on close, and background content stays in the tab order. Group tabs use role=tab/tablist without tabpanel, aria-controls or arrow-key handling.

Map page uses a fixed 440px non-shrinking aside beside a flex-1 min-w-0 map with no responsive breakpoint, and a 250px layer panel over the map; at phone widths the map column collapses. Monitoring has the same pattern with a fixed 250px layer rail.
The main map container has no role or accessible name, and marker/polygon selection, hover popups and all spatial tools are pointer-only (map.on('click'/'mouseenter')).
78 focusable SVG municipio paths remove the focus outline (focus:outline-none) and provide no alternative focus style; they also add 78 tab stops with no roving tabindex.
Basemap Map/Satellite buttons expose the active choice by colour only (no aria-pressed), unlike the other layer toggles. Monitoring range buttons and water-layer rail buttons have the same gap.
Overview and Map routes render no <h1> (neither uses PageHeader); the desktop sidebar's <h2> group headings precede any page heading in DOM order.
WaterDisruption renders its own <main> inside the layout's <main>, producing nested main landmarks.
Mobile header and StatsBar are <div>s; there is no <header>/banner landmark. Backend-down banner has no role=alert/aria-live.

In the mobile drawer the top-level NavLink ignores isActive for styling (always 'text-xl text-sky-700'); the current page is conveyed only by react-router's implicit aria-current, with no visible indication for top-level items.
Several icon-only buttons rely on `title` alone for a name: Review CSV export, Review AI-suggest, Assets CSV export.
Review row selection and 'Select all on page' are plain buttons swapping icons; no role=checkbox/aria-checked/aria-pressed, and every row's button has the same name 'Select record'.

Regulatory 'Approve' is disabled when contradictions exist and the reason is given only through a title attribute on a disabled button (not focusable, not announced); the form itself gives no inline reason for disabled Reject/Needs-review when actor/rationale are empty.
text-slate-500/600 on slate-900/950 backgrounds is still used throughout for captions and metadata (previously measured 3.75:1 in docs/A11Y_AUDIT.md); not re-measured here.
Inline links inside slate-500 paragraph text are distinguished by colour only (no underline).
Controls are sized below 44px by class: h-7 (28px) review buttons, 16px select icons, px-2 py-1 map chips, p-1.5 hamburger.
Recharts charts on Analytics, Overview, Sector and Monitoring have no aria-label, summary or data table alternative (Sector has a separate asset table only).
No prefers-reduced-motion handling in app CSS; map easeTo/fly animations and animate-pulse/animate-spin are unconditional.
Search inputs with placeholder only: Live Logs filter, Outages search, Assets search, ProgramTimeline search; MonitoringCharts 'include polygon' checkbox label UNKNOWN (line 178 not opened in full).
Hand-written tables on Environmental Exposure, Hydromet and Source Intelligence use <th> without scope; Water Use / Hydro Inventory do set scope=row.

special_adjudications.question: 2a. Navigation: sidebar groups and items vs routes
special_adjudications.answer: NAV_GROUPS has 3 groups — Monitor (Overview, Map, Alerts > Outages, Monitoring), Data (Assets, Water & Weather > NWS Hydromet, Aquifer Bands, Water Use, Hydro Inventory; Environment > Cave & Karst; Regulatory > Regulatory Review), Tools (Review Queue, Analytics, Source Intelligence, Live Logs, System & Tools) — 12 rows + 8 sub-links = 20 targets, each matching a route in App.jsx. The 4 parameterised routes (/alerts/:id, /sector/:sector, /events/:id, /municipios/:name) are not in the nav and are reached by in-page links. No nav target lacks a route. One in-page link targets a route that does not exist (/assets/:id). The 'Water & Weather' row label points at /water-disruption, whose page title is 'Water Disruption Validation Console'; 'Regulatory Review' opens a page titled 'Regulatory Link Review'.

special_adjudications.question: 2b. Navigation: mobile behaviour
special_adjudications.answer: Below 768px (window.innerWidth/matchMedia) the sidebar is not rendered until the header hamburger (aria-label 'Open navigation') sets open=true. It then renders a full-screen fixed white <aside aria-label='Navigation'> with a role=tablist of the 3 groups, a round close button (aria-label 'Close navigation') and a <nav> listing the active group's rows as large cards with descriptions and sub-links. Clicking any link closes the drawer; Escape closes it; reopening selects the group containing the current path. Gaps: no role=dialog/aria-modal, no focus move/trap/restore, tabs lack tabpanel/aria-controls/arrow keys, and background content remains reachable.

special_adjudications.question: 2c. Navigation: skip link
special_adjudications.answer: None. No skip-to-content link or equivalent in the layout, index.html or any component (searched 'skip' case-insensitively in dashboard/src and dashboard/index.html; only review 'Skip' controls matched).

special_adjudications.question: 2d. Navigation: landmark structure
special_adjudications.answer: Desktop: <aside> containing <nav aria-label='Main'> with three <section><h2>; one <main> wrapping the route Outlet. Mobile: <aside aria-label='Navigation'> containing <nav aria-label='<Group> pages'>. No <header>/banner and no <footer>; the mobile header and the StatsBar are <div>s outside <main>; the floating AI panel is outside <main> with no landmark or label. /water-disruption nests a second <main>. Overview and Map have no <h1>; other pages get one from PageHeader or their own markup.

special_adjudications.question: 2e. Navigation: current-page indication (aria-current)
special_adjudications.answer: The source never sets aria-current explicitly. All nav links are react-router-dom NavLink, which by library default adds aria-current='page' on the active link (library behaviour, not verified at runtime). Visual indication: desktop rows and sub-links get 'bg-sky-500/15 text-sky-400' when active; on mobile, sub-links get font-semibold but top-level rows have no active styling. Parent rows use prefix matching, so /alerts stays 'active' on /alerts/:id; Overview and Regulatory use `end`. On /outages or /monitoring the parent 'Alerts' row is not marked active (prefix does not match).

special_adjudications.question: 3a. Review Queue (/review): decision controls, names, keyboard, confirmation, failed-write reporting, persistence
special_adjudications.answer: Controls per row: select toggle (button, aria-label 'Select record'/'Deselect record'), AI-suggest (icon-only, title 'Ask AI for a recommendation', no aria-label), Accept (visible text), Reject (visible text), Skip (icon-only, aria-label 'Skip'). Header when rows are selected: 'Approve all', 'Reject all', 'Skip all'; plus 'Select all on page'/'Deselect all'. All are native <button>s, so Tab/Enter/Space work. Global window shortcuts: J/K or arrows move a visual cursor, A/R/S decide the cursor row; ignored only inside input/textarea/combobox/contenteditable. Confirmation: none for single, keyboard or batch decisions; no undo. Optimistic removal with rollback on error (lib/hooks.js:89-101). Failure reporting: a thrown error (401 or network/timeout) shows a destructive toast titled only 'Decision failed' — the error message, which distinguishes 'key missing' from 'key rejected', is discarded. Any other HTTP status is NOT detected: postDecision returns res.json() without checking res.ok, so a 400/404/500 with a JSON body yields the success toast 'Marked <decision>'. Batch reports 'N items processed' regardless of individual failures. Toasts have no live region. Persistence: the backend keeps decisions only in the module-level dict `_decisions` ('survives only until server restart'); nothing is written to outputs/review_queue.json or any ledger, no actor is recorded, and 'skip' is stored but not excluded from GET /review-queue, so a skipped row reappears after the refetch. Authorization: Bearer API_SECRET_KEY when that env var is set, otherwise open.

special_adjudications.question: 3b. Regulatory Review (/regulatory/review): decision controls, names, keyboard, confirmation, failed-write reporting, persistence
special_adjudications.answer: Controls: decision-state filter Select (aria-label 'Filter by decision state'); candidate list of <button aria-pressed>; form with labelled 'Actor' text input and 'Rationale' textarea; three buttons with visible text — 'Approve', 'Reject' (destructive variant), 'Mark needs review'. All native controls, keyboard operable; no shortcuts. Guards instead of a confirmation dialog: all three are disabled until actor and rationale are non-empty and while submitting; Approve is additionally disabled when the candidate has contradictions (reason exposed only as a title attribute). No confirm step and no undo, but a later decision can overwrite. Failure reporting: postRegulatoryLinkDecision throws on 401 (key missing vs rejected), 422 (lists contradiction details) and any other non-2xx ('Decision failed (status)'), and the page shows a destructive toast 'Decision failed' with err.message; rationale is kept on failure and cleared on success. Network errors also reach the catch. Toast has no live region. Read failures are masked: list fetch failures return an empty list so the page says 'No candidates match the current filter'. Persistence: NOT memory-only — the handler writes the decided row (decision_state, decided_at, decided_by, decision_rationale) through write_regulatory_links, which schema-validates and rewrites the links JSONL. Authorization: Bearer API_SECRET_KEY when set.

special_adjudications.question: 4a. GIS: maps present and library
special_adjudications.answer: Three map surfaces. (1) /map AssetMap — maplibre-gl ^6.11.2, raster basemaps from tile.openstreetmap.org and Esri World Imagery, glyphs from demotiles.maplibre.org, AWS Terrarium DEM, optional NOAA/NWS CloudGIS raster overlays; turf.js for spatial tools. (2) /monitoring HydroMapWorkspace — maplibre-gl with OSM raster and backend GeoJSON sources. (3) Overview MunicipalOverviewMap — hand-built SVG choropleth, no map library, no tiles.

special_adjudications.question: 4b. GIS: how layers are toggled
special_adjudications.answer: /map: an HTML overlay panel of native <button aria-pressed> chips — Power, Water, Wastewater, Other, Municipios, Barrios, Events (sample), Alerts, River gauges, Terrain, Spatial tools — plus a single-select municipio fill (Off/Drought/Density/Rainfall, aria-pressed), 'Life-safety critical alerts only' (shown when Alerts on), 'Review-needed assets only', two NWS overlay toggles (aria-pressed, with aria-live load status) and basemap Map/Satellite buttons (no aria-pressed). State is React component state, not persisted. /monitoring: 11 native labelled checkboxes in role=group 'Map layers'. Overview: metric button group (aria-pressed) recolours the SVG.

special_adjudications.question: 4c. GIS: keyboard access to map controls
special_adjudications.answer: All layer/basemap/tool controls are native buttons, checkboxes or a <select>, so they are in the tab order and operable with Enter/Space. MapLibre's NavigationControl (zoom buttons) is added on both maps and the Map constructor does not disable MapLibre's default keyboard handler (library defaults; not observed at runtime). Not keyboard reachable: selecting an asset/alert/gauge/municipio on the map, hover popups, cluster expansion, and the measure/buffer/nearest tools — all bound to pointer events only. The map container on /map has no role or aria-label (HydroMapWorkspace's has aria-label 'Hydrologic map'). The SVG Overview map is fully keyboard operable (tabIndex=0, role=button, Enter/Space) but suppresses the focus outline.

special_adjudications.question: 4d. GIS: non-map alternative for the same data
special_adjudications.answer: Assets: yes — the same page mounts AssetsTable beside the map (keyboard-selectable rows opening the same detail sheet) and /assets offers the full table with an 'unmapped only' filter; the map footer states mapped vs unmapped counts. Alerts: /alerts list. River gauges: /hydromet gauges table. Rainfall fill: /hydromet rainfall table. Municipios: Overview SVG map and /municipios/:name records, but there is no plain municipio list/table and no table of drought category or event density per municipio (the density panel shows only matched/unresolved/total counts). Events: /outages list. Barrios, terrain, NWS radar/warnings overlays: no alternative. Spatial-tool results are text in the tools panel but can only be produced by clicking the map. HydroMapWorkspace layers: /hydro-inventory tables cover aquifers, wells, springs, surface water, infrastructure and wetlands.

special_adjudications.question: 4e. GIS: tile / network failure handling
special_adjudications.answer: /map: no handling for basemap, glyph or terrain tile failure — the only map 'error' listener filters to NWS overlay sources and ignores everything else; there is no offline/blank-basemap message and no try/catch around map construction. Data layers are attached on 'style.load' rather than 'load' so they still draw when raster tiles never arrive (stated in a code comment). NWS overlays do report per-overlay loading/live/error text in an aria-live region, and tile URLs carry a 5-minute cache-busting bucket. Data-fetch failure: event density shows the error with a 'Retry density' button; rainfall error text is passed in as a prop; assets/municipios/alerts/gauges GeoJSON failures silently become empty FeatureCollections (getJSON fallback) and the map just shows fewer features. /monitoring HydroMapWorkspace: construction is wrapped in try/catch ('Map unavailable: …'), every map error (including tile errors) is collected into a role=alert list (max 6), and the offline export shows an explicit placeholder. Overview SVG map: no tiles; shows 'Municipal geometry is unavailable.' when geometry is missing and a contract warning when not exactly 78 features.
